subject: Re: Drafting incident notification & cooperation language for DPA - NovaHealth
messages:
From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@novahealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Apr 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: Incident notification language for DPA

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for hopping on the call last week. NovaHealth is finalizing our data processing addendum and the security/compliance team asked me to confirm the incident notification and cooperation language we should expect from Redwood.

A few specific asks from our side:
- Notification timeline expectations for confirmed vs suspected incidents (we have internal SLA to notify supervisory authority within 72 hours of becoming aware).
- Scope: whether notice includes compromised embeddings/derived outputs, debug logs, and aggregated telemetry.
- Subprocessor disclosure and whether notice extends to incidents involving subprocessors.
- Expected level of cooperation (forensics, evidence sharing, timelines for remediation updates).

Can you share a draft clause we can review and a short note on how Redwood coordinates cross-border transfers (if any logs/forensic data need to be shared with US-based teams)? Attached is our standard questionnaire appendix for reference.

Appreciate it — looking to close this as part of our procurement week.

Best,
Alex Morgan
Security Program Manager
NovaHealth Inc.

Attachment: novahealth-questionnaire-appendix.pdf (PDF - 120KB)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@novahealth.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Apr 2025 11:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Incident notification language for DPA

Alex —

Thanks for the clear list. I pulled together an initial draft and some notes below; Priya and Vivek I’ve looped you in for legal and infra ops nuance.

High-level proposals (draft language follows):
1) Timelines: We propose notifying the customer "without undue delay" and, for confirmed incidents affecting Customer Data, providing initial notification within 48 hours of confirmation. For suspected incidents, notify within 72 hours of detection with an update when confirmation is available.
2) Scope: Notifications will cover any incident that results in unauthorized access to Customer Data, including derived outputs (e.g., embeddings) and debug artifacts that contain Customer Data. Aggregated telemetry that cannot be mapped back to an identifiable customer is excluded.
3) Subprocessors: Redwood will notify Customer within 7 days of becoming aware of an incident at a Subprocessor that impacts Customer Data and will provide contact points and remediation steps.
4) Cooperation: Redwood will provide forensic artifacts, timelines of events, and remediation reports. Where data contains personal data subject to EU law, Redwood will coordinate with Customer on any necessary cross-border transfer safeguards and will only transfer with appropriate legal bases (e.g., SCCs).

Draft clause (for negotiation):
"Incident Notification and Cooperation. Redwood Inference shall notify Customer without undue delay upon becoming aware of a security incident that results in unauthorized access to Customer Data. For confirmed incidents affecting Customer Data, initial notice shall be provided within forty‑eight (48) hours of confirmation of the incident; for suspected incidents, initial notice shall be provided within seventy‑two (72) hours of detection, with an update within forty‑eight (48) hours of confirmation or as otherwise agreed.

Notice shall include: (i) a description of the nature of the incident and the categories of Customer Data affected; (ii) the date and time of detection and, if known, the period of unauthorized access; (iii) actions taken or planned to contain and remediate the incident; and (iv) contact information for Redwood's incident response lead.

If the incident involves a Subprocessor, Redwood shall notify Customer within seven (7) days of becoming aware and shall include any available evidence and remediation steps. Redwood will cooperate with Customer's reasonable requests for forensic information and will provide identified logs, timeline exports, and artifacts necessary for Customer to satisfy regulatory obligations, subject to applicable law and redaction requirements to protect third‑party data and ongoing investigative integrity.

Redwood will coordinate with Customer regarding any cross‑border transfers of personal data necessary for investigation and will implement appropriate safeguards (e.g., SCCs or equivalent) prior to transfer where legally required."

Open questions:
- Priya: is the 48/72 split defensible from a legal exposure standpoint? NovaHealth expects 72 hours to regulator; they may want 24 hours to customer in some cases.
- Vivek: do we have operational constraints around providing raw KV cache or generated embeddings as forensic artifacts (PII redaction, reproducibility)?

I attached a redline (v3) with inline alternatives for the timelines. Happy to hop on a quick call if that speeds this up.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Attachment: DPA_incident_clause_redline_v3.docx (Docx - 24KB)

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Apr 2025 14:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Incident notification language for DPA

Soojin / Vivek —

Quick legal perspective: the 48/72 approach is reasonable but we should clarify definitions and gating language to avoid committing to impossible timing for confirmation. Suggest:
- Define "detection" = first indication of anomalous activity reasonably indicative of an incident.
- Define "confirmation" = completion of initial triage that establishes unauthorized access to Customer Data.

Redline notes (high level):
- Replace absolute 48h confirmation promise with "initial notification within forty‑eight (48) hours of confirmation or, if confirmation is not possible within that timeframe, an initial update within seventy‑two (72) hours of detection describing known facts and estimated next update." This protects us if triage requires more time.
- Subprocessor clause: add a requirement that Redwood use commercially reasonable efforts to procure cooperation from the Subprocessor and provide Customer with remediation timelines; do not warrant the Subprocessor's performance.
- Cross‑border transfers: include explicit reference to SCCs/legally required safeguards and a commitment to provide notice if forensic exports require transfer of personal data outside the EEA.

Also flag: we should avoid promising raw runtime heaps or K/V caches without additional safeguards. Propose: provide logs and timeline exports; raw model parameters or full KV caches to be provided only under a written evidence request and with data minimization/redaction.

I'll attach a quick markup after this and propose we push back on anything that obligates us to produce unredacted system-level dumps.

—Priya
Priya Natarajan
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference

From: Alex Morgan <alex.morgan@novahealth.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 16 Apr 2025 09:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Incident notification language for DPA

Thanks — helpful draft and good points from Priya. A few clarifications from NovaHealth Security: 
- Regulator timeline: we need Customer-internal notification processes to be completed such that our legal team can assess regulator filing within 72 hours. That means receiving an initial incident summary within 24–36 hours in severe cases is ideal. Are you willing to commit to a "high severity" route (initial summary within 24 hours, full initial notice within 48)? We understand confirmed/triage limitations but need faster visibility when event flags indicate sensitive PHI exposure.
- Subprocessors: if the incident originates with a subprocessor in a different jurisdiction, we need a named point of contact and weekly remediation updates until resolved.
- Cooperation: we appreciate the redaction protection; however, NovaHealth requires identified logs and hashes of outputs to assist our internal review — not a full system dump. We can accept hashed artifacts where appropriate.

Would Redwood accept: a two-tier timeline (High / Standard) with clear severity triggers and an explicit weekly update cadence for subprocessor incidents? If yes, we can sign off faster.

Best,
Alex

Alex —

We can accept the two-tier approach. Summary of agreed redlines and next steps: 

Agreed items:
- Severity tiers: 
  * High severity: incidents likely to involve sensitive personal data (e.g., PHI) or widespread unauthorized access — initial summary within twenty‑four (24) hours of detection; full initial notice within forty‑eight (48) hours of confirmation.
  * Standard severity: initial notice within seventy‑two (72) hours of detection with updates as confirmation becomes available.
- Subprocessor incidents: Redwood will notify Customer within seven (7) days of awareness for standard incidents, and within twenty‑four (24) hours for high severity subprocessor incidents. Redwood will provide a named subprocessor contact and weekly remediation updates until resolution.
- Artifacts & redaction: Redwood will provide logs, timeline exports, and hashed artifacts for generated outputs by default. Production-level dumps or raw KV caches will only be provided subject to a separate evidence request and with redaction/minimization where feasible.
- Cross‑border: Redwood will coordinate transfers and use SCCs or equivalent safeguards where transfers of EU personal data are necessary for investigation; Redwood will notify Customer prior to such transfers when feasible.

We uploaded an updated redline (v3) that incorporates these points. Please review and, if acceptable, reply with confirmation and we’ll have legal prepare the final DPA attachment. If you’d like a working session to walk the document, I can book 30 minutes early next week.

Thanks for the quick turn — glad we could land on a practical approach that preserves both regulatory needs and operational constraints.

Regards,
Soojin Lee
Head of Sales, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
